PullRequest.Title: Agents window: align terminal instance list styling
PullRequest.Body:

Aligns the Agents window terminal instance list with the editor window’s Modern UI presentation.

### Changes

- Apply the same inset, rounded terminal rows in default and compact density.
- Match the list background to the Agents panel without overriding drag-target highlighting.
- Add computed-style regression coverage for row geometry, icon-only mode, drop targets, and light, dark, and high-contrast theme classes.

### Validation

- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — passed.
- `npm run build-fast` — passed (full product build).
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/terminal/test/browser/terminalTabsStyles.test.ts --reporter dot` — passed, 10 tests reported by the runner.
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/sessions/contrib/terminal/test/browser/terminalTabsStyles.test.ts` — passed.
- `npm run stylelint -- src/vs/sessions/browser/media/workbench.css src/vs/sessions/browser/parts/media/panelPart.css` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Commit-time hygiene — passed for all three changed files.
- Code review — no significant issues found.
- Launched the built Code OSS Agents window and verified its renderer endpoint. Live visual and keyboard-interaction testing was not recorded.

### How to test

1. Open the Agents window, show Terminal, and create several terminal instances, including a split group.
2. Compare the right-hand instance list with the editor window: rows should have matching inset spacing and rounded corners.
3. Switch between default and compact density and check light, dark, and high-contrast themes.
4. Narrow the list to icon-only mode, navigate it with the keyboard, and drag a terminal onto the list to verify the drop highlight remains visible.

No linked issue was supplied.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open, render, and scroll the terminal instance list in the Agents window
Scenarios.CriticalPath: TerminalTabbedView constructs one TerminalTabList, WorkbenchList renders the visible rows, then the browser performs style calculation, layout, and paint. The diff only adds static left/right/width/border-radius declarations to matching visible terminal rows; the added getComputedStyle calls exist only in the test file and are not on the product path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number of currently rendered WorkbenchList rows, bounded by the terminal-list viewport rather than terminal history or workspace size. The diff adds constant simple styling per matching visible row.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All changed production styling is handled by the browser on the renderer main thread as part of existing list rendering and scrolling. No new tasks, promises, workers, queues, or concurrency bursts are introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The stylesheet and inherited theme variables follow existing browser CSS caching. There is no new application cache, cache key, miss path, negative cache, or coalescing behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: the changed CSS, TerminalTabbedView construction, and TerminalTabList's WorkbenchList ownership were traced directly. The product code contains no changed script path or computed-style read.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact incremental selector-matching and paint cost is browser-dependent, but the selector is narrowly scoped and declarations apply only to existing visible list-row DOM nodes; there is no scaling boundary or repeated script work introduced by the diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The change reuses the same inset-row styling already used by Modern UI and does not add forced layout, extra DOM nodes, per-instance boundary calls, or unbounded retained state.

Scenarios.Scenario: Switch density/theme and drag a terminal over the empty terminal-list area
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Changing a root density/theme class or toggling the existing drop-target class causes normal browser style invalidation and repaint. The new :not(.drop-target) background rule affects one list container, while the pre-existing drop-target rule remains authoritative during a drag.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One terminal list container plus its currently visible rows per state change. Drag state changes do not fan out per terminal instance through new code.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The existing drag handlers synchronously toggle one class on three existing elements; the diff does not add handlers or increase event frequency. Browser style recalculation remains serialized on the renderer main thread.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Theme values are inherited CSS custom properties and resolve through the existing style system. No cold/warm application cache behavior or network/filesystem lookup is added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: the drop-target toggle and both base/new CSS rules were inspected. The diff changes only the resulting paint properties and does not move any I/O or script work onto dragover, theme, or density paths.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser repaint cost varies by platform and terminal-list area, but the changed invalidation covers one existing container and the existing visible rows only; no evidence supports frame-scaling layout work beyond normal CSS repaint.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff preserves the existing drop-target class transition and adds only a static non-drop background and row geometry, with no new synchronous geometry reads, listener fan-out, or expensive boundary.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all three changed files and all diff pages. Traced terminal-list construction, WorkbenchList ownership, browser render/style paths, and drag-target state changes. No actionable performance regression or concrete regression fix was found.
